description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

userStories.title: End-to-end mobile/PWA story: snap → grade → list, offline beyond intake
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I want to capture a garment, grade it, and start a listing from my phone — with the PWA install offered wherever I am and offline support beyond just the intake form — so the mobile experience is a real workflow, not a FlipDesk-only afterthought.
acceptanceCriteria: The PWA install affordance (pwa-install-banner.tsx) is offered outside FlipDesk too (e.g. on snap.tsx / dashboard on mobile) with copy that fits the context
snap.tsx connects into the pipeline: a captured item can flow snap -> grade -> create FlipDesk item, instead of being an isolated 'what's it worth' page
Offline support (currently use-offline-intake.ts for intake only) extends to viewing submission status and certificates while offline; the service worker caches those routes
The mobile capture path reuses the upload validation/EXIF-strip rules (US-276); build + eslint clean
userStories.notes: [P3][Cohesion/Mobile] DEFERRED 2026-06-08 — needs real device/PWA QA, and the audit was partly stale. AC2 ALREADY EXISTS: snap.tsx already has a 'List it with FlipDesk' CTA (-> /dashboard/flipdesk) alongside 'Get a certified grade' (-> /dashboard/submissions/new), so it's not isolated from the pipeline. The rest is genuinely PWA/service-worker/offline work that can't be verified headless: (AC1) pwa-install-banner.tsx is mounted only in flipdesk/intake.tsx and calls ensureServiceWorker() — the SW is DELIBERATELY scoped to FlipDesk intake (vite.config 'service worker not auto-injected app-wide'; only the banner + use-offline-intake register it), so surfacing the install affordance app-wide changes SW registration scope and offline behavior and must be QA'd on a real device + as an installed PWA; (AC3) caching submission-status/certificate routes for offline is a Workbox/SW change whose correctness (cache invalidation, stale auth) only shows on a device. RECOMMENDATION: do this as a focused mobile/PWA session with an actual phone + installed-PWA testing — generalize the banner copy + mount point with intentional SW-scope changes, add Workbox runtimeCaching for the read-only submission/cert routes, and (optionally) a snap-photo -> FlipDesk-intake handoff that prefills the captured image (reusing US-276 validateImageUpload/stripImageMetadata). NOT shipping blind. Depends on [[US-736]].

userStories.title: iOS: single source of truth for Sales + Expenses (retire the Remote* shadow stores)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the money numbers to agree everywhere — today Sales and Expenses are fetched separately from the local cache, so figures can drift and expenses aren't tied to the items they offset.
acceptanceCriteria: Sales and Expenses are read from the shared SwiftData store (cache them like LocalSale/LocalListing) instead of SalesStore/ExpenseStore making independent server fetches of RemoteSale/RemoteExpense
SalesView and MoneyView read the SAME LocalSale source (no Local-vs-Remote split), so P&L/net-profit can't drift between screens
Expenses cache carries an optional inventoryItemId/listingId link so per-item P&L and expense-by-source views become possible
Sync engine populates these; offline reads work; no double-fetch
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Cohesion] DONE (both halves). SALES half (2026-06-08): SalesView reads LocalSale via @Query, same source as MoneyView — no drift. EXPENSES half (this session): new LocalExpense @Model (registered in ModelStoreProvider.schema) mirrors flipdesk_expenses; SyncEngine pulls it (RemoteExpenseRow wire-shape, expenseColumns incl. the new link cols, decodeExpensesResiliently, scoped by ownerId) → SyncMergeActor.mergeExpenses (delta upsert by id, date-only spent_on parse) → SyncWatermark .expenses cursor (schemaVersion bumped 2→3 forces a one-time backfill on existing installs). MoneyView now reads @Query<LocalExpense> for the list + net-profit (expensesThisMonthTotal), no ExpenseStore.refresh — single source, offline-instant, no double-fetch. ExpenseStore.create/delete rewritten to write a client-id row to the server (idempotent) AND mirror into the shared SwiftData cache (online + offline-queue), carrying optional inventoryItemId/listingId. ExpenseFormSheet gained an optional 'attribute to item' picker (+ presetInventoryItemId). LocalExpense added to BOTH ContentView sign-out + workspace-switch local wipes (tenant isolation). AC3 link backed by MIGRATION 00266 (flipdesk_expenses.inventory_item_id + listing_id, nullable FK ON DELETE SET NULL, partial indexes) — applied+idempotent on throwaway PG16, FK-set-null verified; EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 00265→00266 same commit. Tests: ExpenseSyncTests (RemoteExpenseRow lenient amount / optional links / date-only parse / resilient drop). iOS UNVERIFIED here (no macOS/xcodebuild); no-ungated-print passes. Files: migrations/00266, schema-version.ts, Persistence/Models/LocalExpense.swift, ModelStoreProvider, SyncWatermark, SyncMergeActor, SyncEngine, ContentView, Money/{ExpenseStore,MoneyView,ExpenseFormSheet}, GradeThreadTests/ExpenseSyncTests.

userStories.title: iOS: reconciliation link/create refreshes the local cache
userStories.description: As a user reconciling orphan listings, I want a linked/created item to immediately show its listing — today after linking, the item still shows zero listings until who-knows-when.
acceptanceCriteria: After 'Link item' / 'Create item' in ReconciliationView, the local SwiftData cache is updated (optimistically + via a targeted sync) so the item's canvas shows the now-linked listing
The reconciliation list removes the resolved orphan without a full manual re-sync
Failure to link is surfaced (the iOS app currently doesn't confirm the link worked)
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Cohesion] DONE. ROOT CAUSE found: the item canvas shows listings from the `listings` table (LocalListing @Query), but iOS ReconciliationService.createItem/link only flipped flipdesk_ebay_listings.matched_item_id and NEVER wrote a `listings` row — so the canvas showed 0 listings (the WEB reconciliation, src/components/flipdesk/ebay-sku-match.tsx, DOES insert/upsert a listings row on both create + link; iOS didn't). FIX: ReconciliationService now mirrors the live eBay listing into `listings` on create (best-effort — never strands the created item) AND link (surfaces failure → .failed → retry-safe since it's select-then-insert/update), via upsertEbayListingRow + a pure, tested ebayListingMirrorFields(from:) mapping (platform_listing_id=ebayItemId, listing_url/title pass-through, listing_price defaults 0; listing_origin=ebay, listing_status=active, is_active, listed_at only on insert) — RLS scopes listings through the owned parent item, no user_id needed. ReconciliationView.applyOutcome now (1) optimistically drops the resolved orphan [AC2], (2) HapticFeedback.success() confirms it worked, (3) awaits syncEngine.sync() (fallback: .inventoryPullRequested) to land the LocalListing so the canvas shows it [AC1]. AC3 (failure surfaced) was already met by both sheets' inline error alerts; Create's redundant notification post removed (centralized). Tests: ReconcileListingMirrorTests (pass-through + price-defaults-0 / nil-safe). iOS UNVERIFIED here (no macOS/xcodebuild); no-ungated-print passes. Files: Marketplaces/Reconciliation/{ReconciliationService,ReconciliationView,CreateItemFromListingSheet}.swift, GradeThreadTests/ReconcileListingMirrorTests.swift.

userStories.description: As an iOS user hitting a plan cap, I should get an upgrade prompt instead of a raw error. Knowledge docs are editable by admins (reuse the content knowledge admin surface).
Educational sections cite real platform capabilities/links (no invented claims), enforced in the prompt.

userStories.title: AI newsletter copywriter (new email content surface)
userStories.description: As the platform, I want Claude to autonomously write a complete weekly newsletter — subject line(s), preheader, and the section copy (what's new, teach-something, tip, CTA) — reusing the content-ai prompt architecture, so no human writes the email.
acceptanceCriteria: New lib/content-ai-email.ts generates a structured JSON issue (subject + 2-3 subject variants, preheader, intro, sections[] each with heading/body/optional image_prompt/optional cta, footer note) via getAnthropicClient() through ai-limiter, with a versioned prompt (email_issue_v1) in content-ai-prompts.ts.

The system prompt assembles the email.voice/structure/value_props knowledge docs + the issue's inputs (changelog entries, chosen educational topic, KB tip) + compact history context, mirroring content-ai-blog.ts.

Output is validated/normalized (lengths: subject <=60 chars, preheader <=110 chars), sanitized, and persisted to a newsletter_issues table (migration) with status draft, model_used and token counts recorded.
Copy is grounded strictly in the provided inputs — no fabricated features, stats, or links (negative test asserts the model can't invent a feature not in the changelog input).
Dedup: the chosen topic + a distilled summary append to content_history_index on send so future issues don't repeat.
Generation is idempotent per issue id and safe to retry.

userStories.title: Email-safe modular HTML rendering engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want the generated issue JSON rendered into bulletproof, email-client-safe HTML (table layout, inline CSS, dark-mode aware, Outlook/MSO compatible, mobile responsive) using branded components, so emails look right everywhere without a human touching HTML.
acceptanceCriteria: New lib/email-render.ts turns issue JSON into HTML using table-based, inline-CSS components (header/logo, hero, article-card section, tip callout, CTA button, divider, footer) in the GradeThread brand palette, replacing reliance on the minimal emailLayout for marketing.

Output passes email-client constraints: all CSS inline, no <style>/JS reliance, MSO conditional comments for Outlook buttons, max-width 600px, fluid/responsive, prefers-color-scheme dark handling, and web-safe/Inter fallback fonts.
A plaintext multipart alternative is auto-generated from the issue (deliverability + accessibility).

Every image has alt text and explicit width/height; every link is absolute and gets wrapped by the click-tracker at render time; the CAN-SPAM footer + preference-center + List-Unsubscribe are always present.
A render-snapshot test asserts stable, valid HTML for a sample issue and that no relative URLs or <script> survive.
Components are reusable so lifecycle/drip emails share the same look.

userStories.title: AI-generated, email-safe imagery
userStories.description: As the platform, I want each issue to have on-brand hero/section images generated and hosted automatically, so emails are visual without a designer — and the images render in email clients (hosted PNGs, absolute URLs, alt text).

Cost is bounded per issue (configurable max images) and counts toward the AI spend dashboard / budget guardrails.

userStories.title: Per-recipient personalization blocks
userStories.description: As a user, I want the weekly email to feel relevant to me — a quick recap of my own activity (items graded, listed, sold this week) and a tailored next-best-action — so the newsletter drives me back into the product, not just generic news.
acceptanceCriteria: A personalization resolver computes per-recipient dynamic blocks at send time from existing data (grades used this week, items listed, sales, slow-movers, trial days left, credits balance) without N+1 — a single batched query per send batch.

The renderer injects an optional 'your week on GradeThread' block and a tailored CTA (e.g. 'you have 3 ungraded items', 'your trial ends in 2 days'); recipients with no activity get an evergreen variant.
Personalization respects privacy/consent and never leaks another user's data; merge fields have safe fallbacks so a missing value never renders 'undefined'.
Personalized blocks are token-substituted into the pre-rendered template (not re-generated by AI per user) to keep cost O(1) per issue.
A test renders the issue for a high-activity and a zero-activity user and asserts correct, non-leaky output.
Personalization can be toggled per issue (some broadcasts are non-personalized).

acceptanceCriteria: New lib/newsletter-assembler.ts orchestrates: select audience-appropriate unsent changelog entries -> pick a deduped educational topic from the bank -> generate copy (content-ai-email) -> generate imagery -> render HTML+plaintext -> persist a complete newsletter_issues row (status='ready_for_qa').

Cadence + balancing: at most one issue per configured interval; product-focus/audience balancing so grading-only vs FlipDesk users get relevant content (reuse the content-scheduler balancing approach).
Graceful degradation: if there's no fresh 'what's new', the issue leans on evergreen educational content rather than skipping or inventing news.
The assembler is idempotent (one issue per period key) and resumable if a sub-step fails, with each step's status recorded on the issue.
All AI calls route through ai-limiter and count toward AI spend/budget.
Config (cadence, audiences, max images, sections) lives in a newsletter settings singleton (mirrors content_settings).

userStories.title: Autonomous pre-send QA / guardrail gate
userStories.description: As the platform, I want every issue to pass automated quality and safety checks before it can send, so a fully autonomous pipeline never ships a broken, off-brand, or non-compliant email.
acceptanceCriteria: A QA gate runs on each issue before send and blocks on failure: all links resolve (no 404/relative), all images load and have alt text, unsubscribe + preference-center + postal address present, plaintext alternative exists, subject/preheader within length, no spammy-words/ALL-CAPS/excessive punctuation beyond a configurable spam score, and no leftover template/merge-field placeholders.
An AI 'editor' pass (cheap model) checks brand-voice + factual grounding against the issue inputs and flags hallucinated claims; a hard flag blocks send.
Outcome: pass -> issue becomes 'approved' (auto-send) OR 'awaiting_review' when the settings 'require_human_approval' toggle is on; fail -> 'blocked' with reasons + an ops alert.
Results (each check, pass/fail, details) are stored on the issue and shown in the admin console.
A seed-corpus regression test feeds known-bad issues (broken link, missing unsubscribe, hallucinated feature) and asserts each is blocked.
Thresholds live in the settings registry so they're tunable without deploy.

userStories.title: Durable segmented marketing send via outbox
userStories.description: As the platform, I want approved issues delivered to the right segment reliably — through the durable email_deliveries outbox with retry, honoring suppression and consent, idempotently — so sends survive transient failures and never double-mail.
acceptanceCriteria: Sending an approved issue enqueues per-recipient rows that flow through the email_deliveries outbox (category='newsletter') so marketing mail gets the same retry/backoff/dead-letter durability as transactional (closes the US-627 gap where broadcasts had no durable retry).

Recipient resolution = target segment (segments.ts iterateSegmentUsers) UNION confirmed email_subscribers, de-duped by email, MINUS suppressions MINUS users without newsletter consent; each decision recorded as sent/skipped(reason) in campaign_recipients with the UNIQUE(campaign_id,user_id,channel) idempotency guard.

The send is a durable, resumable server-side batch bounded per tick (reuse the bounded-batch pattern from US-407/US-559), honoring the SES warmup rate limiter; a re-run never re-sends an already-sent recipient.
Per-recipient personalization + click-tracking rewriting happen at enqueue/render time.
Each issue links to its campaign_recipients ledger for analytics.
Tenant/consent test: a suppressed or opted-out address is skipped and recorded, never sent.

Cadence guard ensures no recipient gets more than one newsletter per period even across re-runs.
The weekly schedule, timezone handling, and per-period cadence are config-driven (no code change to move the send day).
Wired into the jobs console (US-881) with last-run/next-due visibility.
A holiday/quiet-period pause toggle can skip a week without breaking the cadence counter.

userStories.title: Subject-line & content A/B testing with auto-winner
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want the system to A/B test subject lines (and optionally hero/CTA) on a holdout, pick the winner by open/click, and send the winner to the rest — automatically — so emails keep improving without manual experiments.
acceptanceCriteria: Each issue can carry 2-3 subject variants (already produced by the copywriter); the sender allocates a configurable test fraction across variants, waits a configured measurement window, then sends the winning variant (by open, or click for CTA tests) to the remainder.
Variant assignment + per-variant open/click are recorded on campaign_recipients (variant column) and rolled up per issue.
Winner selection requires a minimum sample size, else falls back to a default variant (no spurious winners on tiny lists).
The whole flow is autonomous (no human picks the winner) but visible/overridable in the admin console.
A test simulates opens across variants and asserts the higher-performing subject is chosen and sent to the holdout.
Works through the same durable outbox + idempotency guarantees.

userStories.description: As the platform, I want open/click/unsubscribe signals to feed back into what we send — favoring topics, subject styles, and send times that engage — so the autonomous program gets smarter over time.
acceptanceCriteria: An analysis job aggregates per-issue and per-topic engagement (open rate, CTR, unsub rate) and per-subject-style and per-send-hour performance.

Topic selection in the assembler is biased toward higher-engaging pillars/angles (and away from high-unsub ones) via a weighting it reads from the aggregates; subject-variant generation is nudged toward winning styles; send-time optimization consumes the per-hour stats.
Guardrails prevent runaway narrowing: exploration floor so under-tested topics still get airtime; unsub-rate ceiling that pauses a topic.
Recommendations + the current weights are surfaced in the admin console for transparency/override.
All tuning is data-driven from the engagement tables (no manual inputs required) and documented.
A test asserts a topic with a high unsub rate is down-weighted in the next selection.

userStories.description: As the platform, I want automated lifecycle email series triggered by user state — onboarding welcome, trial-ending nurture, and win-back for inactive users — reusing the same generation/rendering/send stack, so engagement isn't only the weekly broadcast.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds email_journeys + email_journey_steps (trigger enum(signup,trial_ending,inactivity,first_grade,first_sale), step offset days, template ref) and enrollment tracking so each user advances through a series once.

A daily evaluation job enrolls users whose state matches a trigger (e.g. signup -> welcome series; trial_ends_at within N days -> nurture; no activity for N days -> win-back) and sends the due step via the durable outbox, honoring consent + suppression.

Step content reuses the email-render components and may be AI-personalized; transactional vs marketing classification is correct (welcome can be lifecycle-transactional; win-back is marketing and respects opt-out).
Enrollment is idempotent and exit conditions stop the series when the goal is met (e.g. user converts -> stop trial-nurture).
Trial-ending nurture finally closes the long-standing gap where the trial-expiry cron downgrades users without warning them.
Admin can view/enable each journey; metrics roll up per step.

userStories.title: Internal behavioral event stream (trigger substrate)
userStories.description: As the platform, I want key user actions recorded to an internal events table the drip engine can query, because server-side PostHog (posthog.ts) only fires OUT to analytics and there's no internal store to trigger journeys from. This is the substrate every behavioral trigger reads.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds user_events (id, user_id, event_key, properties jsonb, occurred_at, dedupe_key nullable unique) indexed on (user_id, event_key, occurred_at).

A lib/user-events.ts emitEvent() helper records events at the existing action sites alongside (not replacing) posthog.capture(): signup, first_grade, grade_completed, first_listing, listing_published, sale_recorded, checkout_started, subscription_created, trial_expired, login/app_open (for activity).
A derived last_active_at per user is maintained (cheap: updated from app_open/grade/listing events) so 'inactivity' triggers don't need expensive joins; expose it to segments.ts as a new field.
Emission is fire-and-forget and never blocks or fails the originating action; first-occurrence events (first_grade, first_listing) are idempotent via dedupe_key.
RLS: service-role only; user_events is never client-exposed.
A backfill seeds first_grade/first_listing/signup timestamps for existing users so current trialists can enroll correctly.
userStories.notes: [Trial Conversion Drip Engine / Trigger Foundation] Added 2026-06-12. Trial=14d, no-card (grade-pricing.ts); conversion=customer.subscription.created (webhooks.ts); drop-off=trial-expiry cron->Free. Drip runs ~28d (14 in-trial + 14 post-trial win-back), exits instantly on conversion. Builds on/supersedes the generic US-929 journey engine. Reuses: email_deliveries outbox + US-925 send, US-911 consent, US-913 open/click tracking, US-914 suppression, US-918 copywriter + US-919 renderer + US-921 personalization, US-927/928 A/B + self-tuning, segments.ts predicates, admin coupons, jobs console US-881. userStories.title: Trigger & condition engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want a unified trigger engine supporting event-based triggers (first_grade), anchor-relative time triggers (trial_ends_at minus 2 days, signup plus N days), and state/condition predicates (subscription_status, feature-used, inactive N days), so drip steps fire on exactly the right signal. Generalizes the simple daily check sketched in US-929.
acceptanceCriteria: A trigger spec supports three kinds: event (user_events key), time-anchor (anchor field +/- offset; anchors: signup/created_at, trial_ends_at, enrolled_at, last step sent), and state predicate (reuse the segments.ts field/op/value compiler for conditions like subscription_status != active, last_active_at within_days).
An evaluator resolves, for a given user/enrollment, whether a trigger is due now, combining a step's trigger with AND-conditions and skip/branch conditions.
Time anchors handle nulls (no trial_ends_at) and timezones safely; an event trigger can be 'has occurred since enrolled_at'.
The evaluator is pure/testable in isolation with a table of fixtures (trial ends in 2 days -> due; already graded -> skip the nudge; converted -> exit).
Reuses segments.ts predicate compilation rather than a parallel rule language.
No external calls in the evaluator; it operates on a loaded user/enrollment snapshot.

userStories.title: Marketing frequency cap & cross-program send coordination
userStories.description: As a user, I don't want to be bombarded across the trial drip, lifecycle journeys, and the weekly newsletter, so the platform must cap and coordinate all marketing email per recipient with clear precedence.
acceptanceCriteria: A central pre-send check enforces a per-recipient marketing frequency cap (default max 1 marketing email/day, configurable in the settings registry) across ALL marketing sources (trial drip, journeys, weekly newsletter, win-back).
Precedence rules: while a user is enrolled in the trial drip, the weekly newsletter is paused for them (drip wins); transactional mail is never capped.
When the cap would be exceeded, the lower-precedence send is deferred (re-queued) rather than dropped, so content isn't silently lost.
Quiet-hours support (no marketing sends outside a configurable window in the recipient's timezone) with a safe default.
All marketing senders (US-925 outbox, journeys, drip) route through this coordinator; a test asserts two same-day marketing sends collapse to one + a deferral.
Consent (US-911) and suppression (US-914) are checked here as the single chokepoint.

userStories.title: Branching drip campaign data model
userStories.description: As the platform, I want drip campaigns modeled as a graph of steps with per-step triggers, delays, conditions, branch targets, and exit conditions, replacing the linear email_journey_steps from US-929 with a real branching state machine, so sequences can adapt to behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds drip_campaigns (key, name, goal_event, audience, is_active, settings jsonb) and drip_steps (campaign_id, step_key, trigger spec, send_template ref, conditions, on_skip_goto, on_branch rules, is_exit) — or extends US-929's email_journeys/steps with these columns; pick one and document that US-929's three series become drip_campaigns in this engine.
A step references a renderable template (reuse the US-919 email-render components + US-918 copywriter output) and carries variant slots for A/B (US-927).
Goal/exit is first-class: a campaign declares its goal_event (subscription_created) and any step can be a branch/exit; reaching the goal exits the whole campaign.
Steps validate into a DAG (no infinite loops); a loader compiles a campaign into an in-memory graph for the engine.
Seed the 'trial_conversion' campaign shell (steps filled by the sequence stories) plus migrate welcome/win-back from US-929.
RLS service-role only; admin reads via /api/admin/*.

userStories.title: Enrollment & state-machine engine
userStories.description: As the platform, I want durable per-user enrollment that advances each user through their drip based on triggers, evaluates branches, and exits on goal/unsub/suppress, idempotently and resumably, so the autonomous sequence runs reliably.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration adds drip_enrollments (user_id, campaign_id, status enum(active,completed,exited,paused), current_step_key, enrolled_at, next_evaluation_at, context jsonb) with UNIQUE(user_id, campaign_id) so a user enrolls once per campaign.

An enrollment evaluator (lib/drip-engine.ts) loads due enrollments, evaluates the current/eligible steps via the trigger engine, sends the due step through the coordinator+outbox, advances current_step_key (honoring branches/skips), and exits on goal/unsub/suppress/end.

Enrollment is created when a user matches a campaign's entry trigger (e.g. signup -> trial_conversion); evaluation is idempotent (a step is sent at most once per enrollment, guarded by a sent-steps ledger).
Processing is a bounded, resumable server-side batch (reuse US-407/US-559 pattern) safe to re-run; a crash mid-batch never double-sends.
Exit reasons are recorded (converted/unsubscribed/suppressed/completed) for analytics.
Tests: a trialist who converts on day 8 exits and receives no further drip steps; a dormant trialist gets the inactivity branch.

userStories.title: Conversion attribution & goal tracking
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want every subscription conversion attributed to the drip step/email that drove it, so I can measure what the sequence is worth and which messages convert.
acceptanceCriteria: On subscription_created (webhooks.ts) the engine resolves the user's active trial_conversion enrollment, marks it converted, records last-touch attribution (last drip email opened/clicked before conversion) and first-touch, plus days-to-convert and which step.
An attribution row links conversion -> campaign -> step -> email send, and rolls up to the analytics dashboard (US-946).
Conversion immediately triggers exit + a 'Welcome to Pro' confirmation email and pauses all win-back/nurture for that user.
Attribution tolerates users who converted without opening any drip email (records 'unattributed/organic').
Revenue (plan MRR) is associated with the conversion for ROI reporting.
Idempotent: a duplicate subscription webhook doesn't double-count a conversion.

userStories.title: Phase 1 activation sequence (days 0-6)
userStories.description: As a new trialist, I want a helpful onboarding/activation sequence in my first days so I experience the product's value fast, increasing the odds I convert. Implements the in-trial activation steps of the trial_conversion campaign.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed steps on the trial_conversion campaign: Day 0 welcome + 'grade your first item' (trigger signup); Day 1 first-grade nudge (trigger T+1d AND NOT first_grade, skipped if first_grade occurred); Day 2 'how grading lifts resale price' value email (trigger first_grade event); Day 3 'accurate listing management' education; Day 5 social-proof + feature highlight.

Each step's copy is generated/rendered via the US-918 copywriter + US-919 renderer from a per-step brief (goal, key points, CTA) stored on the step, grounded only in real platform capabilities (no invented claims).
Branch: an inactivity nudge fires if the user has no activity for 3 days during the trial (last_active_at), inserted without breaking the main timeline.
CTAs deep-link into the exact next action (grade an item, create a listing) with tracking.
Copy is personalized where useful (name, items graded so far) with safe fallbacks.
Steps respect the frequency cap and exit-on-conversion universally.

userStories.title: Phase 2 conversion-push sequence (days 7-14)
userStories.description: As a trialist approaching the end of my trial, I want a personalized recap and clear, urgent reasons to subscribe before I lose Pro, so I convert rather than lapse. Implements the conversion-push steps tied to trial_ends_at.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed steps: Day 7 mid-trial personalized recap + ROI framing (their activity to date); Day 10 deep-dive on a high-value feature they haven't used (branch: skip if used); Day 12 'trial ends in 2 days' urgency (trigger trial_ends_at - 2d); Day 13 'ends tomorrow / what you'll lose' (trigger trial_ends_at - 1d); Day 14 'last chance today' (trigger trial_ends_at).
Urgency steps are anchored to the actual trial_ends_at (not a fixed offset) so an admin-adjusted trial window (admin-billing.ts) stays correct.
The recap pulls real per-user numbers (grades, listings, sales, certificates) via the personalization layer; a zero-activity trialist gets a re-activation variant instead.
Each email's primary CTA is 'add a card / subscribe' deep-linked to the Stripe checkout for their recommended plan.
Steps clearly state what Pro features are lost on downgrade (grounded in plan-gate.ts entitlements).
Convert-at-any-point exits the sequence and stops further urgency emails.

userStories.title: Phase 3 post-trial win-back sequence (days 15-28)
userStories.description: As a lapsed trialist now on Free, I want a respectful win-back sequence that reminds me what I'm missing and makes upgrading easy, so I can still convert after the trial. Implements the post-trial win-back steps.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed steps for users whose trial expired to Free (trial_expired event / subscription_status none): Day 16 'you're on Free now - here's what you're missing'; Day 20 value/objection-handling email; Day 24 incentive offer (see US-945, config-gated); Day 28 final win-back, then exit to the general weekly newsletter.
Entry is conditioned on NOT converted and NOT suppressed/opted-out; users who converted during the trial never enter win-back.
Frequency/quiet-hours/consent all enforced; win-back is unambiguously marketing and fully honors unsubscribe.
On exit (day 28 or conversion), the user is handed back to the standard newsletter cadence (newsletter un-paused).
Copy emphasizes outcomes and the specific Pro features they used during trial (from user_events) for relevance.
A test asserts a converted user is excluded and an opted-out user receives none.

Checkout CTA pre-applies the promo so conversion is one click; redemption attributes to the incentive in analytics.
Guardrails: incentive respects a max-discount and an eligibility check (e.g. only post-trial, never to already-paid), enforced server-side.
Turning the incentive off cleanly reverts the Day-24 email to the value-only variant.
Admin can configure/enable the incentive from the drip builder; changes audited + step-up.

userStories.title: Autonomous orchestration tick (trigger cron)
userStories.description: As the operator, I want one scheduled trigger (Make.com/cron) that runs the whole drip engine autonomously - enroll new trialists, evaluate triggers, advance steps, send due emails, exit on goal - with zero per-message human input.
acceptanceCriteria: New POST /api/drip/tick (auth mirrors content-scheduler.ts: X-Internal-Job-Secret OR admin JWT, constant-time) that: enrolls users matching entry triggers, evaluates active enrollments, and dispatches due steps via the bounded resumable batch.
Job-locked (no overlapping runs), idempotent, and frequent-safe (self-gates on next_evaluation_at) so the Make schedule can be simple (e.g. hourly).
Each run records to the jobs console (US-881) with counts: enrolled, advanced, sent, exited, skipped.
Time-anchor triggers (trial_ends_at - 2d) are honored within the tick granularity; a missed window (downtime) is caught up on the next run, not skipped.
Secrets via env (DRIP_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET); no hardcoding.
A dry-run mode logs what WOULD send without sending, for safe verification.

userStories.title: Per-step A/B testing + conversion self-tuning
userStories.description: As a marketer, I want drip steps to A/B test subject/content/send-timing and automatically favor what drives conversions (not just opens), so the sequence improves itself over time.
acceptanceCriteria: Each step supports variants (subject/body/CTA/send-offset); the engine assigns variants per enrollment and records variant + outcome (open/click/convert) on the send ledger.
Winner selection optimizes for the goal (conversion, with click as a secondary signal), requires a minimum sample, and falls back to a default below threshold (no spurious winners on small cohorts).
Self-tuning reuses the US-928 closed-loop machinery: step timing/subject style weights shift toward higher-converting variants with an exploration floor.
All tuning is autonomous and data-driven, but visible and overridable in the builder.
Tests: across simulated cohorts, the higher-converting variant becomes the default and a high-unsub variant is retired.
Attribution (US-944) feeds the optimizer.

userStories.title: In-browser camera capture for web grading submission
userStories.description: As a seller grading on mobile web, I want to shoot photos directly inside the submission flow instead of leaving for the phone camera, so grading is one continuous action. Today src/components/submission/photo-upload.tsx is file-input only, so each of the 4 required slots forces a leave-app/find-file/return round-trip on mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: Each photo slot offers a 'Take photo' option (getUserMedia/WebRTC) on camera-capable devices, alongside the existing file picker.
Captured frames run the SAME client compression + EXIF extraction and server validateImageUpload() path as uploads (no bypass).
Permission denied or unsupported browser falls back gracefully to the file input with a clear message (no dead-end).

For listing_origin='gradethread', do NOT overwrite eBay-owned editable fields (title, price, quantity, description, specifics); update only read-only signals (views, watchers, listing_status when sold/ended, orders/sales, fees).
GradeThread-owned fields (grade, condition report, measurements, cost/source, sku) are never written by the pull for either class.

The eBay source_of_truth per-field pin (pinnedAgainstEbay / US-148) is removed from the pull path; verify sheet-sync.ts does not depend on listings.source_of_truth before deprecating the column (keep column, stop writing/reading it from eBay pull; mark deprecated in a comment).

userStories.title: Google Sheets bidirectional exemption: document + guardrails + tests
userStories.description: As the team, we keep the existing bidirectional Google Sheets sync (it can overwrite populated DB fields by design), but it must NOT overwrite eBay-owned fields on eBay-originated (locked) listings, and those cells must be surfaced to the user as skipped items rather than silently dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: Sheet sync behavior is left bidirectional (3-way merge, DB-wins conflicts) for everything EXCEPT eBay-owned fields on eBay-originated (listing_origin='ebay') listings - no other functional downgrade.
During a Sheets pull, a sheet edit to an eBay-OWNED field on an eBay-originated (locked) listing is NOT applied to the DB (eBay remains source of truth; the next eBay sync would overwrite it anyway).

Each such non-applied cell is recorded as a 'skipped item' in the sync result/summary (count + per-row/field detail), reusing the existing skipped-reporting surface so the user sees what was not synced and why ('locked - edit on eBay').
GradeThread-owned fields and unowned fields on the same locked listing still sync normally; the skip is field-scoped, not row-scoped.

The exemption + skip rule is documented in SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md and in code comments at the sheet-sync entry points; confirm sheet-sync does not rely on listings.source_of_truth (deprecated by US-1078).
tsc/lint/build green; deno lint/check/test green for edge changes.

userStories.title: Eliminate silent SwiftData save failures across the offline/sync layer
userStories.description: As a reseller working offline, I want my queued edits, photo uploads, and merged server data to never be silently lost, so that what the app shows me is what is actually persisted.

A persistent local-write failure (e.g., disk full, store corrupt) surfaces a user-visible "changes could not be saved locally" signal instead of appearing to succeed
PhotoUploadService no longer orphans a server upload when the metadata insert AND the fallback pending-mutation insert both fail silently
Unit tests cover save-failure paths (injected failing ModelContext) for the mutation queue and merge actor

userStories.title: Harden StoreKit Transaction.updates: unverified, revocation/refund, and pending handling
userStories.description: As a paying customer, I want refunds, async renewals, and interrupted purchases to be reflected correctly, so that I am never charged without entitlement or left on a paid tier after a refund.
acceptanceCriteria: The `Transaction.updates` listener no longer silently `continue`s past `.unverified` transactions — it breadcrumbs them and reports for server-side reconciliation instead of dropping them
Client checks `revocationDate`/`revocationReason` (refund/revoke) and proactively clears the cached entitlement + triggers a server sync rather than waiting for the next fetch
Server report failures from the listener are retried with bounded backoff (or re-queued) rather than the transaction being finished best-effort with the result discarded
A `.pending` purchase (Ask-to-Buy / SCA) surfaces a clear "purchase pending approval" state and the entitlement is granted when the listener later receives the approved transaction
Unit/integration coverage via a StoreKit test configuration for: verified grant, unverified, revoked, and pending paths
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS/Billing][EPIC: iOS Production Readiness 2026-06-21]

userStories.title: Retry HTTP 429 rate-limits with Retry-After backoff and breadcrumb them
userStories.description: As a user during peak load, I want rate-limited requests to back off and retry instead of failing instantly, so that grading polls and eBay sync do not error out spuriously.
acceptanceCriteria: `EdgeAPI.isTransient` treats `.rateLimited` (429) as retryable (currently only `.network` + `.serverError` retry)
Honor a `Retry-After` header when present; otherwise use the existing bounded exponential backoff
Idempotent GET/poll paths (grade polling, eBay sync) retry on 429; non-idempotent writes are handled per their own idempotency guarantees
429 events are recorded as scrubbed Sentry breadcrumbs so rate-limit frequency is visible to support
Unit test: a 429 then 200 succeeds after backoff; retries are bounded by `maxRetries`
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Networking][EPIC: iOS Production Readiness 2026-06-21]

userStories.title: Route all AI/edge clients through EdgeAPI hardening + fix unsafe write retries
userStories.description: As a user on a flaky network, I want every AI/edge call to get the same retry, token-refresh, and plan-gate handling as the rest of the app — and I never want a failed write double-applied — so that AI features are as robust as core flows and I'm not charged/listed twice.
acceptanceCriteria: AIExtractService and SizeAIService route through EdgeAPI (or a shared base) so they inherit retry/backoff, 401 token-refresh, and X-Plan-Warning plan-gating instead of hand-rolled URLSession paths
EdgeAPI no longer blindly retries 5xx on non-idempotent POSTs — either restrict 5xx retry to idempotent methods or attach a client-generated idempotency key header so the server can dedupe
Force-unwrapped URLComponents(url:resolvingAgainstBaseURL:)! in AIExtractService, SizeAIService, ProspectService, ScoutService, CompsService are guarded (throw a network error, no crash)
EdgeAPI also honors the HTTP-date form of Retry-After (not just delay-seconds)
Build + unit tests clean; add a test asserting POST is not retried on 5xx without an idempotency key
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS/Networking][IMPORTANT][EPIC: iOS Launch Readiness Deep-Dive 2026-06-21] Two AI services bypass EdgeAPI hardening; 5xx retry on POST risks duplicate sales/listings. Headless-codeable. PARTIAL 2026-06-21 (correctness+crash-safety DONE; full routing DEFERRED, passes stays false): DONE — EdgeAPI no longer blind-retries 5xx on non-idempotent POST/PATCH (new shouldRetry(_:method:) + isIdempotent; 429/network still retry any method; +test asserting POST 5xx not retried); parseRetryAfter now honors the HTTP-date (RFC 1123) form, clamped >=0 (+test); guarded all 7 force-unwrapped URLComponents in AIExtractService/SizeAIService/ProspectService/ScoutService(x2)/CompsService/SnapService (throw instead of crash). DEFERRED — routing AIExtractService + SizeAIService fully through EdgeAPI to inherit retry/token-refresh/plan-gating: that needs an EdgeAPI per-call decoder option (these decode camelCase 1:1, not the snake_case shared decoder) + auth/plan-gate behavior verification, an architectural change best done on CI. Pending iOS CI compile. || COMPLETE 2026-06-25: AC1 — AIExtractService + SizeAIService now route through EdgeAPI.aiShared.sendRaw (new AI-session-backed EdgeAPI instance + new sendRaw data-in/data-out entry point that runs the shared transient-retry/backoff, one forced 401 token-refresh, and X-Plan-Warning/402 plan-gate loop while letting the AI clients keep their verbatim-key codec). perform() refactored to encodeBody + performRaw + decode so the typed and raw paths share one loop. AC2 — shouldRetry(_:method:) already restricts 5xx retry to idempotent methods (done previously). AC3 — force-unwrapped URLComponents already guarded across AIExtract/Size/Prospect/Scout/Comps (done previously). AC4 — parseRetryAfter already honors the HTTP-date form (done previously). AC5 — EdgeAPITests gains behavioral test_500_on_POST_isNotRetried (attempted once) + test_500_on_GET_isRetried + sendRaw auth/raw-bytes + sendRaw 401-refresh tests. NOTE: Swift uncompiled (macOS-only); iOS CI is the safety net.

userStories.title: Batch/parallelize bulk operations and fix O(n^2)/unbounded list paths
userStories.description: As a power seller with hundreds of drafts/imports, I want bulk edits and big lists to be fast and bounded, so that the app doesn't hang behind one spinner, scan O(n^2) per render, or silently hide rows past a cap.
acceptanceCriteria: Drafts bulk field-apply / bulk-edit writes are bound-parallelized (TaskGroup with a small concurrency cap) collecting per-item failures, instead of one sequential round-trip per draft
DraftsBulkEditView indexes rows by id ([String:Int]) for O(1) lookup/writes instead of store.rows.first{...} per field per render; the grid uses a lazy container
CSV import inserts are chunked/batched with per-chunk error mapping back to row numbers, with an enforced max file size/row cap and a friendly reject on oversized files
Drafts pagination: filter batch_id server-side (not client-side after a 500 cap) or surface a 'showing first N' notice
Scout/AutoLister result lists use LazyVStack; CompsService static categoryCache is bounded (NSCache/LRU) and doesn't cache empty responses; EdgeAPI cache eviction avoids per-entry O(n) min()
Build + unit tests clean
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Performance][IMPORTANT][EPIC: iOS Launch Readiness Deep-Dive 2026-06-21] Sequential bulk writes, O(n^2) draft grid, 500-row silent cap, eager lists, unbounded caches. Headless-codeable. PARTIAL 2026-06-21 (perf-correctness wins DONE; parallelization DEFERRED, passes stays false): DONE — DraftsBulkEditStore now keeps an id->index map so the grid is O(1) per field read/write (was O(n^2) via first(where:)); ScoutView results use LazyVStack (AutoLister reviewList already did); CompsService category cache is bounded (FIFO cap 200) and skips empty responses; EdgeAPI cache eviction sorts once by recency instead of O(n) min() per drop; CSV import rejects files >5MB (pre-read size check) and >20k rows; DraftsLibrary shows a "most recent drafts" notice when the 500-row fetch cap is hit. DEFERRED — parallelizing the sequential Drafts bulk field-apply writes and the CSV per-row inserts (TaskGroup): both currently work correctly (just sequential); parallelizing safely involves @Sendable existential-service captures + the CSV seenSkus dedup dependency, which carry compile/runtime risk best verified on CI. List is already a lazy container. COMPLETED 2026-06-21: the deferred parallelization is now done. DraftsLibraryStore.applyBulk saves in bounded-concurrency chunks (cap 4) via withTaskGroup, folding results back on the @MainActor store (the production DraftsService is a stateless struct so parallel saves are safe; the test FakeService.saved is now NSLock-guarded). InventoryImportService.commit splits into a sequential SKU-dedup pre-pass + chunked parallel inserts (cap 4), preserving row-ordered per-item error reporting; friendly() made nonisolated static. Project has no warnings-as-errors and 11 existing Task.detached usages, so the non-Sendable existential captures are warnings only. Pending iOS CI compile.

userStories.title: iOS: offline UPDATE/DELETE replay must not run ahead of a still-pending CREATE (silent data loss)
userStories.description: flushPending() (SyncEngine.swift ~764-785) drains queued mutations FIFO but does NOT stop on failure: apply() catches all errors and calls markFailed (SyncEngine.swift ~821-824), then continues to the next mutation. So when an item is created offline (queued) and then edited offline (queued), if the CREATE is failing/stuck, the later UPDATE runs UPDATE ... WHERE id=... against a row the server does not have yet. PostgREST returns HTTP 200 affecting 0 rows (no error), apply() treats it as success and dequeues the mutation — the user edit is permanently lost with nothing surfaced. Same for an UPDATE/DELETE that sails through after its CREATE exhausts the 6-retry budget.
acceptanceCriteria: UPDATE/DELETE replays for a targetId cannot flush ahead of a still-pending CREATE of that same id (dependency ordering), OR
replayUpdate requires Prefer: return=representation and treats 0 affected rows as a retryable failure rather than success
A CREATE that is failing/stuck blocks (or defers) dependent UPDATE/DELETE mutations for the same row instead of letting them dequeue against nothing
A regression test reproduces create-then-edit-offline with a failing create and asserts the edit is not lost
userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/DataLoss] ADDED 2026-06-24 (iOS app audit). Found by a multi-agent deep-dive audit; verified against real code (file:line in description). NOT yet implemented. || DONE 2026-06-25: flushPending now defers UPDATE/DELETE replays whose CREATE is still queued (incl. stuck creates past the retry budget) via unconfirmedCreateTargetIds/shouldDeferDependent; apply() returns success so a confirmed create unblocks dependents in the same pass. Prevents the 200/0-rows silent edit loss. +4 unit tests (SyncTests). Pending iOS CI compile.

userStories.title: iOS: delta watermark must not advance past resiliently-dropped rows (permanent row loss)
userStories.description: SyncEngine.pull advances each cursor to the max updated_at of SUCCESSFULLY DECODED rows (SyncEngine.swift ~168-172), while decodeItemsResiliently / the Failable wrapper (~693-710) silently drop undecodable rows. If a page contains a row that fails to decode sitting at a lower updated_at than rows that decode cleanly, the watermark jumps past it — the dropped row is now permanently below the cursor and never re-fetched on any delta pull (only a full backfill on sign-out or schema-version bump recovers it). This is a silent data-loss window distinct from US-1003 (which only logs the drop).
acceptanceCriteria: The watermark advances to the max of the raw JSON page (jsonArrayCount already parses it), not just the decoded subset — OR is clamped to min(maxDecoded, minDroppedTimestamp - epsilon) so a dropped row keeps the cursor behind it
A row that fails to decode is re-fetched on the next delta pull once decodable, rather than requiring a full backfill

userStories.title: iOS: Realtime must follow the active workspace, re-subscribe on switch, and catch-up pull on reconnect
userStories.description: Three related realtime gaps. (1) The Realtime channel is scoped to the signed-in user (RealtimeService.swift ~75/82-86 filters user_id={selfUserId}) while pulls scope to WorkspaceScope.activeOwnerId ?? selfId; .workspaceDidChange (ContentView.swift ~136-140) resets watermarks but never touches realtimeService, and the guard `channel == nil else return` (~67) blocks re-subscription — so a workspace member gets live updates only for their OWN rows, never the owner workspace. (2) applyStatus (~196-210) maps socket status to a UI phase only — nothing triggers a catch-up pull() on the .subscribing->.subscribed transition, so events emitted during a disconnect (token expiry, cellular handoff, backgrounding) are lost until the next foreground. (3) clearLocalTenantCache (ContentView.swift ~283-293) deletes Local* rows but not LocalPendingMutation.
acceptanceCriteria: The Realtime channel is scoped to WorkspaceScope.tenantOwnerId(selfId:) and is torn down + re-subscribed on .workspaceDidChange (stop() then start(userId: activeOwnerId))
Every .subscribed transition (including re-subscribes after a drop) kicks a SyncEngine.pull() to reconcile any events missed during the gap
Workspace switch clears or correctly re-homes LocalPendingMutation so a queued mutation from the prior workspace does not flush unexpectedly into the new one
A member switched into an owner workspace sees another member's concurrent edit without a manual refresh
userStories.notes: [P2][Sync/Realtime/Workspace] ADDED 2026-06-24 (iOS app audit). Found by a multi-agent deep-dive audit; verified against real code (file:line in description). Pending iOS CI compile.

userStories.title: iOS: surface photo-upload failures at the capture -> AI handoff (don't route to canvas silently)
userStories.description: startIntakeFlow (PhotoIntakeView.swift ~756-765) enqueues uploads then immediately sets draftItemId and presents AIExtractView. AIExtractView advances to onComplete() purely off the EXTRACTION phase (AIExtractView.swift ~51-55), never inspecting uploadStore task phases; onComplete dismisses + deep-links to the canvas (PhotoIntakeView.swift ~230-243). The only per-slot upload-retry affordance (retryUpload, ~799-805) is destroyed on dismiss. So if a photo upload fails (flaky network, expired token, iCloud-not-downloaded) the item is created and the user is whisked to the canvas with no warning — then the grade flow later blocks on requiredPhotoTypesMissing with no explanation of why a photo they captured is "missing." US-998/US-1001 cover timeout-warning and DB-link-insert retry, not this AI-handoff completion check.
acceptanceCriteria: Before firing onComplete, the flow checks uploadStore for .failed tasks on this item and surfaces a "Some photos didn't upload — retry?" prompt (or carries the failure into the canvas with a visible banner + retry)
onComplete is gated on uploads reaching a terminal state, or upload failures are explicitly announced rather than silently dropped
A user can recover failed uploads without losing the captured photos
The downstream grade blocker no longer presents a "missing photo" the user actually captured but failed to upload

userStories.title: iOS: Scout/Prospect 402 plan-gate must route to the upgrade/paywall flow, not a dead-end retry
userStories.description: The app has a centralized 402 -> UpgradePromptView -> PaywallView path (PlanGateNotifier.swift ~76-82, PlanGatePresentation.swift ~49-51) but it only fires for calls routed through EdgeAPI. Scout (ScoutService.swift ~94-128) and Prospect (ProspectService.swift ~73-82) roll their own URLSession transport and decode the gate body into a string-only error. A free user entering ScoutAI/Prospect (primary monetization surfaces) is told to "upgrade in Settings" with no tappable path, and the only button ("Try again", ScoutView.swift ~160-171) loops the same failure — an entitlement-gating conversion hole distinct from US-1116 (transient network retry).
acceptanceCriteria: On HTTP 402, ScoutService.send and ProspectService.send decode via PlanGateError and route to PlanGateNotifier.shared.present(gate) — the same hook EdgeAPI uses
Feature-lock (402) errors present the upgrade/paywall flow with a working CTA, not a "Try again" that re-runs the gated call
The useless "Try again" is suppressed for feature-lock errors (still shown for transient network errors)
Routing Scout/Prospect through EdgeAPI (or sharing its 402 handling) is preferred over the bespoke transport if feasible

userStories.title: iOS: multi-account eBay correctness — sync poller and bulk pricing target the right connection
userStories.description: Two multi-account (US-671) correctness bugs. (1) EbaySyncService.fetchConnectionSnapshot (~210-222) selects the active eBay connection by created_at DESC limit 1, but the edge /listings/pull advances the PRIMARY connection (flipdesk-ebay.ts ~2620 orders is_primary DESC) and EbayConnectionService.fetchActiveConnection also uses is_primary DESC. If the primary store is not the most-recently-created connection, the sync modal polls the wrong row's last_synced_at -> didAdvance stays false -> the modal hits .timedOut after 90s even though sync succeeded (and masks a real refresh_error on the primary). (2) BulkPricingService (~81-102) lists listings filtered only by platform=ebay + active (no account scoping) but the edge bulk endpoint pushes every update through the PRIMARY token (flipdesk-ebay.ts ~3488-3491) — so with two stores, secondary-store listings fail or collide on same-SKU offers, with the UX silently mixing accounts.
acceptanceCriteria: fetchConnectionSnapshot orders by is_primary DESC, updated_at DESC to mirror the edge token resolver and fetchActiveConnection (no false sync timeout for multi-store users)
Bulk pricing scopes its listings query to the selected/primary connection (by marketplace_connection_id where present), or the account is made explicit in the UI so users don't mix stores
A multi-store user can run sync and bulk pricing without per-row failures caused by account mismatch
Behavior is verified with two connected eBay connections where the primary is not the newest

DEFERRED — AC2 scoping bulk pricing to the selected/primary connection: the listings table has NO marketplace_connection_id / connection_id column (verified across supabase/migrations), so listings cannot be scoped to a store at the iOS query layer; the real fix needs a listings->connection FK (migration + edge), not iOS-only. || COMPLETE 2026-06-25: AC1 done previously (fetchConnectionSnapshot orders is_primary DESC, updated_at DESC). AC2 — taken via the AC's explicit alternative path ('or the account is made explicit in the UI so users don't mix stores'), since the listings table has NO marketplace_connection_id column: BulkPricingService.ebayAccounts() reads the user's active eBay connections (RLS-scoped, ordered is_primary DESC/updated_at DESC like the edge token resolver); BulkPricingStore exposes hasMultipleAccounts + primaryAccountName; BulkPricingView shows an info banner naming the PRIMARY store every bulk edit routes through, with a pointer to switch it in Marketplaces -> eBay accounts. AC3 — multi-store users can no longer unknowingly mix accounts. AC4 — ordering mirrors the edge resolver. Tests: BulkPricingValidationTests gains a FakeProvider + single/multi-account banner cases. userStories.title: iOS: AI-extract conflicts and Size-AI department must be surfaced/persisted, not silently picked or discarded
userStories.description: Two AI-attribute dead-ends that feed mis-sized listings (a top reseller pain). (1) AI extraction conflicts (text-vs-photo disagreements) are decoded (AIExtractTypes.swift ~31-43, ~110/162) but applyResponse (AIExtractStore.swift ~119-148) consumes everything EXCEPT response.conflicts, and AIFillReviewSheet has no conflict UI — so when tag OCR and photo vision disagree on size/brand, the app silently resolves to whichever value landed in suggestions, defeating the documented two-candidate review affordance. (2) Size AI infers gender/department and shows it in a transient OK-only alert (ItemCanvasView.swift ~948-987) but only writes r.size — the inferred department (an almost-always-required eBay aspect) is discarded when the alert dismisses, so the listing ships without it.
acceptanceCriteria: AIExtract conflicts are threaded through to AIFillReviewSheet with a two-candidate picker per FieldConflict (or, at minimum, size/brand conflicts prefer the tag value at lowered confidence so they land in the opt-in review list)
Size AI persists an inferred department via AIItemFieldWriter (source "ai:size", confidence r.confidence) alongside the size write, instead of only showing it in a transient alert
No high-error field (size/brand/department) is silently resolved without either user choice or persistence
Unit coverage for conflict threading and department persistence

manifest.json is written with .completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication and its directory is created with the .protectionKey attribute

userStories.title: iOS: fail-closed OAuth state nonce on RNG failure + remove JWT-at-rest in the background upload session
userStories.description: Two crypto/secret-handling hardening items. (1) EbayConnectionService.generateStateNonce (~240-247) discards the SecRandomCopyBytes return value (`_ =`); on CSPRNG failure the buffer stays all-zeros and emits a predictable base64 state — the client-side CSRF defense for the eBay connect callback degrades to a constant. The SIWA path right next door does it correctly (SignInWithAppleCoordinator.randomNonce ~27-28 uses precondition on the result). (2) PhotoUploadService (~252-261, ~74-86) sets Authorization: Bearer <jwt> on a request handed to a BACKGROUND URLSession, which serializes the full request (headers included) to the system background-transfer DB on disk outside the Keychain; queued requests built with a now-expired token also 401 on resume with no refresh path (PhotoSignedURLProvider avoids this with an ephemeral session).
acceptanceCriteria: generateStateNonce fails closed: guard SecRandomCopyBytes(...) == errSecSuccess and abort the connect (or precondition) instead of returning a zero/predictable nonce — mirroring the SIWA pattern

The background photo upload no longer persists a long-lived bearer JWT in the background-session task DB: prefer a short-TTL signed/pre-authorized upload URL (no Authorization header), or refresh-and-rebuild the request on resume
Expired-token uploads on background-session resume have a refresh/retry path rather than a silent 401
Both behaviors are covered by tests where feasible
userStories.notes: [P2][Security/Crypto] ADDED 2026-06-24 (iOS app audit). Found by a multi-agent deep-dive audit; verified against real code (file:line in description). NOT yet implemented. || PARTIAL 2026-06-25 (AC1 done, passes stays false): DONE — generateStateNonce now fails CLOSED: guards SecRandomCopyBytes==errSecSuccess via precondition (mirrors SignInWithAppleCoordinator.randomNonce) instead of discarding the result, so a CSPRNG failure can no longer emit a predictable all-zero OAuth state nonce. DEFERRED — AC2 removing the bearer JWT from the BACKGROUND upload session: the correct fix (mint a short-TTL Supabase signed-UPLOAD URL so the background request carries no Authorization header) reworks the PRIMARY capture->upload flow and is too risky to do blind; needs device/CI verification. The expired-token-on-resume retry path AC already holds today: a 401 on the background upload routes through handleNetworkFailure -> pending mutation -> SyncEngine.replayUploadPhoto re-uploads with a fresh token on an ephemeral (non-persisted) session. || COMPLETE 2026-06-25: AC1 done previously (generateStateNonce precondition fails closed on CSPRNG failure). AC2 — the background photo upload no longer stamps a long-lived bearer JWT onto the request the background URLSession serializes to its on-disk task DB: new SignedUploadURLProvider mints a short-lived single-object signed UPLOAD url (POST /storage/v1/object/upload/sign/{bucket}/{path}) over an ephemeral (non-persisted) session, and PhotoUploadService.start() PUTs to it with NO Authorization header (token rides in the query string). New StorageURL.uploadSign endpoint + PhotoUploadService.backgroundUploadRequest static builder make the no-credential invariant unit-testable. AC3 — a mint failure (incl. expired token) fails closed and routes to handleNetworkFailure -> pending mutation -> SyncEngine replay re-mints, so a background-resume 401 has a retry path, not a silent failure. AC4 — SignedUploadURLTests covers the endpoint shape, resolve, mint-request, and the no-Authorization-header invariant; nonce randomness already covered. NOTE: Swift uncompiled (macOS-only); iOS CI is the safety net.

userStories.title: iOS: bulk-pricing input validation — reject >=100% reductions and computed price <= 0
userStories.description: BulkPricingStore (~56-77) validates priceValue only as v > 0 (no upper bound). In .reduce mode targetPrice = row.price * (1 - v/100), so entering 100 yields 0.00 and >100 yields a negative price; the local guard never catches it (it checks the absolute input, not the computed result). The eBay edge rejects price <= 0 (flipdesk-ebay.ts ~3441) so it fails server-side, but the user gets a confusing per-row "Failed" with no reason, and a 99% reduction to a few cents silently succeeds.
acceptanceCriteria: In .reduce mode the percent is constrained to 0 < v < 100 with inline feedback
The computed targetPrice is floored (reject < 0.01) before building the update, with a row-level message
A 100%/150% reduction is blocked client-side with a clear explanation instead of a generic server "Failed"
Unit test covers reduce-mode bounds

NOT yet implemented. || DONE 2026-06-25: bulk-pricing reduce-mode bounds. priceValue now constrains .reduce input to 0<v<100 (100% zeroes / >100% goes negative); priceInputError gives inline feedback; validatedTargetPrice floors the COMPUTED price (reject <$0.01 with a row reason) so a deep reduce on a cheap item is blocked client-side instead of an opaque server 'Failed'. apply() surfaces preflight row reasons. +6 unit tests (BulkPricingValidationTests).

userStories.title: iOS: sync hygiene — delete/tombstone propagation, watermark the listings full-pull, consistent flush/pull order, classify replay retries
userStories.description: A bucket of delta-sync hygiene gaps (each distinct from prior sync stories). (1) Sales/expenses/listings/photos merges are upsert-only (SyncMergeActor mergeSales ~192-236, mergeExpenses ~243-276, mergeListings ~283-323; photos prune only on full backfill), and Realtime delete handling exists only for inventory_items (RealtimeService ~146-148) — so a row deleted server-side lingers forever, inflating Money totals, dashboard rollups, and the widget snapshot. (2) listings is re-fetched in full (up to 50k rows) on every pull (SyncEngine ~541-547, watermark: nil) — the one un-watermarked table, O(total listings) per pass (distinct from US-986 which optimized the merge fetch). (3) The connectivity path flushes-then-pulls but manual sync() pulls-then-flushes (SyncEngine ~88-91 vs ~124-130), creating a nondeterministic resurrection/clobber window. (4) markFailed burns the shared 6-retry budget for permanent replay errors (missingTarget/missingLocalFile/invalidStorageURL) the same as transient network failures (~822-824, ~1046-1064).
acceptanceCriteria: Server-side deletes propagate to the local mirror for sales/expenses/listings/photos (deleted_at tombstone the delta acts on, periodic id-reconciliation, or extend Realtime delete handling to those tables)
listings is watermarked on updated_at like inventory_items (latest-price derivation fed from the delta + cached LocalListing rows) instead of a full pull every pass
Both connectivity and manual sync paths use the same order (flush-then-pull) so local intent is pushed before server state merges down
Replay errors are classified: terminal SyncReplayError cases mark stuck/needs-attention immediately without consuming the transient retry budget; only network/5xx consume retries
userStories.notes: [P3][Sync/Hygiene] ADDED 2026-06-24 (iOS app audit). Found by a multi-agent deep-dive audit; verified against real code (file:line in description). NOT yet implemented. || PARTIAL 2026-06-25 (2/4 ACs done, passes stays false): DONE — AC3 consistent flush-then-pull order (sync() now flushes before pulling, matching the connectivity debouncer); AC4 replay-error classification (SyncReplayError.isTerminal -> markStuck pins retryCount to maxRetries immediately for missingTarget/missingLocalFile/invalidStorageURL, so terminal errors no longer burn the 6 transient retries; notSignedIn/storageUpload stay transient). DEFERRED — AC1 server-side delete/tombstone propagation for sales/expenses/listings/photos and AC2 watermarking the listings full-pull both need a price-derivation reshape (latest-price from delta + cached LocalListing) + prune-correctness that should be device/CI-verified, not done blind.

userStories.title: Coverage scoring engine — which garment zones the photos actually document
userStories.description: As a seller, when I submit photos I want the system to compute which standard inspection zones of the garment are visible, so the grade — and any guarantee — is scoped to what was actually documented (LiDAR-style coverage, but from 2D photos so it works for every device).
acceptanceCriteria: New lib services/edge-functions/src/lib/coverage.ts defines per-garment-type inspection-zone templates keyed off garment_category (e.g. front, back, collar/neckline, cuffs L/R, hem, underarms, pockets, primary closure/zipper, interior lining, branding/care label)

The grading pipeline maps each submitted image to one or more zones using existing per-image vision view/zone signals (ai-grading.ts), producing covered_zones[], missing_zones[], and coverage_pct (0-100)
Zones a garment type does not have (e.g. no pockets) are excluded from the denominator, not counted as missing
Coverage result persisted on the grade report via an idempotent migration (IF NOT EXISTS, applied_migrations footer, bump EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION in the same commit)
Unit tests cover a fully-documented set (~100%), a front-only set (low %), and a category with legitimately absent zones
userStories.notes: [P1][Coverage] Keystone for the coverage-gated guarantee (US-1279/1280). 2D zone-based so it works on every device; true 3D/photogrammetry is the separate premium US-1281. Added 2026-06-26 strategy session.

Frontend consumes the coverage engine output (US-1276); no duplicate zone logic in the client
build + eslint clean

userStories.notes: [P1][Coverage][Guarantee] The legal/technical backbone of the grade-fee-back guarantee. Depends on [[US-1276]]. Pairs with [[US-1280]]. Added 2026-06-26.

userStories.title: Grade Accuracy Guarantee remedy — refund the grading fee + free re-grade
